reason: Attempt 1 checked batched-vs-native agreement element-wise at 1e-4 on the first batch of the run only. It passed on c39 (2.0e-5) and failed on c20 (0.0049), stopping the run. Attempt 1 ran with the process defaults (float32 matmul precision 'highest', cuDNN TF32 allowed). A diagnostic on 16 PANC-1 sets showed: with TF32 ('high') per-cell elements differ by up to 0.070 and cell means by 1.1e-4 across batch shapes; with full float32 elements differ by up to 0.002 and cell means by 4.4e-6. Attempt 2 pins full float32 (matmul 'highest', cuDNN TF32 off), runs the check on every context's first batch, and applies the 1e-4 tolerance to the per-condition cell mean, which is the analysed quantity. Under attempt 2 the c20 element-wise maximum is again 0.0049 (attention reduction order) while its cell mean agrees to 1.1e-5, so the element-wise criterion of attempt 1 was mis-specified rather than revealing a semantic difference.
earlier_correction: An earlier version of this note attributed the c20 failure to TF32; the attempt-2 rerun under pinned full precision reproduced the same 0.0049 element difference, so that attribution was wrong and is corrected here.
